problems.problem: Redundant brand messaging: 'TOM FORD' appears in the logo lockup AND again as the first two words of the title directly beneath it (logo bbox y82-113, title y170-210), creating stacked duplicate text at the top. Professional references (Dior, Jo Malone) use one dominant brand voice. Additionally the title at size 60 spans x104-977, nearly full-bleed with only ~104px margins, feeling cramped rather than luxurious.

Contact detail crop (geometry [268,1105,811,1355]) shows the base DOES touch the surface with a visible shadow, so contact is not absent — but the shadow is diffuse and hazy (blur 10 spreads it into a smudge rather than a crisp grounding cue seen in the Dior reference). Slight tightening is needed; offset_y=0 is correct and must not be moved.

The horizontal tonal transition band in the ivory-to-beige gradient cuts across the bottle at mid-height, reading as a shelf/wall seam rather than a smooth seamless sweep. The spec asks for continuous matte floor merging smoothly into the wall; the current transition is too abrupt and visually interferes with the dark glossy silhouette.

The layout is competent but generic: centered bottle plus centered footer subtitle duplicates the label text 'EAU DE PARFUM' (already legible on the bottle), adding no hierarchy. Compared to references, the poster lacks a secondary visual or typographic tension; generous negative space is used correctly, but the bottom third feels empty except for redundant text.

changes.value: Empty warm ivory seamless cyclorama studio environment, broad diffused frontal illumination wrapping evenly, one continuous smooth matte surface flowing from floor into wall with no visible seam or horizon band, gentle cream tonal gradient from pale ivory at top to warm beige at bottom, low-contrast soft falloff, calm quiet minimal atmosphere with generous negative space
